newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: UPS may move Dutch sorting to Brussels.
newsitem.headline: UPS may move Dutch sorting to Brussels.

text.p: United Parcel Service is considering moving its Dutch domestic sorting operations to its hub in Brussels, said UPS public affairs manager, Jan Palmboom.
"The Dutch sorting operation is a very small part of our business so we are considering whether it would be more efficient to combine it with our larger operation in Brussels."

In Amsterdam, the sort comprises two main periods of activity. In a few hours every evening, export consignments and intra-European parcels are sorted out. Some airfreight consignments go via Cologne and some are sorted for ground transportation, he said.
Early morning, deliveries from Cologne are sorted out. These are divided into 30 trucks from Amsterdam.
It is likely that those people that are employed in this sorting in Amsterdam can be offered alternative jobs, he added saying most people are employed on a temporary basis.
"This move would make things more efficient and cost-savings mean that prices can go down which means more parcels and more work for everyone."
For economic purposes it is a good idea, but there are questions concerning UPS guaranteeing other jobs and if the works council agrees, he added.
UPS is in negotiations with the Amsterdam works council. The process could take between one and six months, he added.
Palmboom stressed that it still not a definite plan.
Around 600 people work for UPS in the Netherlands. - Reuters Air Cargo Service Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+5017
